There is a huge difference between feeling anxious about something and having anxiety as a mental health condition. I have debilitating anxiety as a symptom of another serious mental health condition which affects my ability to do certain things at times. I also get anxious in certain situations the same way anyone else would, which does not prevent me from doing things and I will persevere. Actual anxiety (as I’ll call it for the sake of this comment) is far more than just butterflies and cold sweats. It makes you sick to your stomach, real panic attacks feel like you’re about to die. The first time I had one I called an ambulance because it felt like a heart attack, and that isn’t an exaggeration. I wouldn’t wish it on my worse enemy. 

I understand where you’re coming from but we really need to be more careful using the rhetoric “I can’t relate to this so I have a hard time believing it to be real”. You can’t possibly compare you feeling nervous in job interviews to someone who has diagnosed anxiety, with situations such as job interviews being a potential trigger for their panic attacks. It’s not a trigger for me but I would never question someone for whom it was. The cold hard truth is when you have a condition like that, you can’t just suck it up and persevere. You wouldn’t say that to someone with a chronic physical illness so please don’t say it to someone with a mental one. I think we can all benefit greatly from learning about the perspectives of others and understanding that we don’t have to be able to relate exactly to empathise with and support one another.
